items.title: Australian women and children with links to ISIS forced to head back to camp in Syria
items.description: A group of Australian families with links to Islamic State fighters are forced to turn around after leaving a camp in Syria to try and begin their journey home to Australia

items.title: Kidnapped Guthrie's family, friends in FBI's sights, says ex-FBI consultant
items.description: As the FBI continues searching for kidnapped 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie in the United States, a former FBI negotiator says they will be focusing on the grandmother's social circle and family.

items.title: Taylor fails to offer original housing plan, denies knowledge of Ley immigration plan
items.description: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor says he does not know anything about Sussan Ley's proposed immigration policy and that "more supply" is key to solving Australia's housing crisis.

items.title: Coles accused of 'planned' campaign to mislead Australians
items.description: Supermarket giant Coles is accused of a "planned" campaign to mislead customers over discounts on the first day of a bombshell Federal Court case.

items.title: Flotilla of foreign fishing boats spotted in Torres Strait
items.description: A surge in suspected illegal fishing activity puts the Torres Strait and Far North Queensland on high alert, with residents reporting multiple foreign vessels.

items.title: Live: Women's curling kicks off day 10 of the Winter Olympics
items.description: Curling, alpine skiing and short-track skating are all on the agenda early in Milano-Cortina as the Winter Olympics continues. Follow live.

items.title: Bondi Beach gunman Naveed Akram fronts court for the first time
items.description: Bondi Beach gunman Naveed Akram, who is charged with 15 counts of murder, has appeared via video link for the first time in a Sydney court as a senior magistrate extended existing suppression orders in the case.

items.title: Firearms charges laid amid search for Gus, police say unrelated to disappearance
items.description: Detectives investigating the case of missing boy Gus Lamont have made an arrest during their renewed search for evidence – but say it does not relate to his disappearance.

items.title: Nine times Aussie pollies have gone viral, from Katter's croc claim to the misogyny speech
items.description: From the downright weird to the speech that soared, Australia's politicians are under constant scrutiny. What are some other moments when the politician has become the meme?

items.title: Police make 'very strange' appeal for return of kidnapped 85yo Sydney man
items.description: Detectives believe Chris Baghsarian was mistakenly snatched from his bedroom just after 5am on Friday by intruders who forced their way into his North Ryde property.

items.title: Terminally ill man allegedly murdered by wife 'wanted to be done', stepson tells trial
items.description: Kylie Truswell-Mobbs has been committed to stand trial for the murder of her husband David Mobbs, who had motor neurone disease, after he was allegedly given a fatal dose of medication.

items.title: Heat and storms give rise to extreme fire forecast in Victoria
items.description: Almost half the state is expected to face extreme fire conditions tomorrow due to a mix of heat, dry fuels and gusty afternoon storms.

items.title: The right wing has seized control of the Liberals, but the fight has just begun
items.description: Angus Taylor says he will unite the Liberal Party, but a deeper rift is forming between those who want to overhaul the party's direction and those who believe doing so would mean political death.

items.title: Lawyer slams fines given to dive company that left brothers at sea
items.description: Perth Diving Academy Hillarys is fined almost $20,000 after an Australian Maritime Safety Authority probe found it took the crew on board 10 minutes to realise two divers had been left behind.

items.title: Gold Coast 'can't stop growth' but needs 185,000 new homes
items.description: The Gold Coast council plans to push more high-density housing inland to cope with a population surge to 1 million, amid warnings infrastructure is not keeping up.

items.title: Quiz: Can you pass our history test?
items.description: Abraham Lincoln's career advice, Karl Marx's co-author and a Hollywood star's surgery: How well do you know history?

items.title: Intermittent fasting 'no better than doing nothing at all', review finds
items.description: Intermittent fasting has become a popular phrase in dieting, promising health benefits including kickstarting metabolism and helping shed body fat but a major review suggests the diets may be over-hyped.

items.title: AI got personal last week, and it's more complicated than we think
items.description: A fake news story about me, a series of AI breakthroughs and a resignation in the tech world show that 2026 could be pivotal for AI.

items.title: Death of 'beautiful souls' puts police chases under scrutiny
items.description: Lee Casuscelli and Maureen Crosland died when their car was hit in Camden by an allegedly stolen car that police had been pursuing.

items.title: Pepper spray and threat of 'sonic weapons' at protests alarm rights groups
items.description: Alarmed by a spike in pepper spray use and threats of sound cannons at protests, human rights groups want a review of "less lethal" weapons for crowd control.

items.title: Murder accused's affair triggered marriage breakdown, court hears
items.description: A Perth court hears a woman who was allegedly murdered by her husband 40 years ago initiated separation proceedings in 1985, the year before she went missing.

items.title: Candidates announced for NT by-election, CLP pick stumbles on policy questions
items.description: More candidates for the Nightcliff by-election are announced, with Phil Scott running as an independent and the Country Liberal Party preselecting Anjan Paudel, who has stumbled while answering basic policy questions.

items.title: Fisherman mounts rooftop protest over WA demersal fishing bans
items.description: A Geraldton fisherman locks himself to the roof of a government building — and says he has swallowed the key — in a protest over Cook government restrictions.

items.title: Trans rights advocates say Cairns report is no justification for restricting services
items.description: Advocates have called for for better regional services after a Cairns children gender clinic was restricted following a scathing report.

items.title: Alleged museum heist 'like something from a Simpsons episode', magistrate says
items.description: Miguel Simon Mungarrieta Monsalve has been charged with a range of offences after he allegedly broke into a Caboolture museum on Friday morning.
